captions.detailed: This 3D model consists of two separate rectangular connector housings: a taller female socket and a shorter male plug. The female socket features a deep, hollow rectangular cavity on one end to receive the male plug, along with two small square wire contact holes passing through its side wall. The male plug is a solid block with a stepped base and two square recessed wire channels running through its main body.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD script for male and female wire connectors tailored for LED strips. The user should be able to adjust the connector dimensions, outer wall thickness, wire channel width, and contact separation to ensure a tight friction fit.
captions.factory: The design uses a helper module, contact_channel, to subtract two parallel rectangular wire paths from both parts using cubes. The female module is constructed by taking a large outer cube and using the difference operator to subtract a socket cavity (cube) and the contact channels. The male module is built from a union of two cubes to form the stepped plug and base, followed by subtracting the contact channels with appropriate offsets.
